# Rules for this project (read first)

_nextop 0.1.3_

This is a Nextop Agentic Workers project: AI workers are blocks connected by lines, sharing
items through file servers. The framework (`nextop`) is installed as a library; this folder holds
only definitions and project code.

## Golden rules

1. **Never edit the installed `nextop` package.** Everything is changed here, in this folder.
2. **Never edit `runs/`** (run records) or any `workers/*/knowledge_index/` (built by the program).
3. **Keys only in `.env`**, never in code or JSON. `project.json` names the variable (`key_env`, `{env:NAME}`).
4. **After every change run `nextop check`.** It must print `OK` before a run.
5. Sentences the framework sends to the LLM come from its language packs (`"language"` in
   `project.json`); do not copy them into personas. Personas may be written in any language.
6. Names of files, folders, ids and file servers: lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `-`. File server names start with a letter.

## Layout

```
project.json        format, name, language, defaults, adapters
.env                API keys (not committed)
workers/<id>/     one folder per worker        -> workers/README.md
tools/<name>.py     shared tools                     -> tools/README.md
adapters/<file>.py  project adapters (LLM, index, embedding code) -> adapters/README.md
functions/<name>.py function blocks (no LLM)         -> functions/README.md
flows/<name>.json   blocks and lines                 -> flows/README.md
file_servers/<name>/file_server.json  file servers and share lines      -> file_servers/README.md
docs/               .md documents to pick as domain knowledge (the studio lists them)
runs/               run records, written by nextop   -> runs/README.md
```

## project.json

- `language`: `en` or `ko` (the language of framework sentences sent to the LLM).
- `adapters`: named parts by kind: `llm`, `index`, `embed`.
  An entry is `"module:Class"` or `{"class": "module:Class", "options": {...}}`; a relative
  `env_file` option is resolved against this folder.
- Built-in adapters: `nextop.adapters.openai_compat:OpenAICompatLLM` (OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs)
  and `nextop.adapters.http_embed:JsonEmbed` (any JSON embedding API, set up by options only).
- `models`: the (model, server) pairs this project uses, `[{"name": "<model>", "llm": "default"}]`; every model
  choice on the studio uses this list. One model may sit on several servers (one entry per server). A worker's
  `model` and `llm` must match one entry exactly (`nextop check` stops the run otherwise); when you change a
  worker's model, change its `llm` to that model's server too.
- `max_input_chars` on a model entry (max input characters; optional positive integer, none = no limit):
  `{"name": "<model>", "llm": "default", "max_input_chars": 120000}`. Before every LLM call of a worker the
  characters of the whole input are counted (system part, chat history, input sections, tool results so far, tool
  definitions as JSON; image data is not counted). Over the limit, an open question first drops the oldest chat
  history messages (run event `history_dropped`); if it still does not fit, or in an assigned task, the block fails
  with the limit, the total and the largest parts by name and size (e.g. `input section "narration" 41,200 chars`,
  `tool result #7 source_get 18,000 chars`), so you know what to shrink.
- Vision models: mark them on the LLM adapter, `"options": {"features": {"<model>": ["vision"]}}`;
  only they see pictures from file servers.
- Search index for domain knowledge and file servers (optional): the core has no index engine. Write one as a
  project adapter, a file in `adapters/` (see adapters/README.md), and add it as a named entry:

```json
"index": {"<name>": {"class": "adapters.<file>:<Class>", "options": {"...": "what its __init__ takes"}}}
```

  Workers and file servers then name the entry: `"knowledge": {"index": "<name>"}`, `"index": "<name>"`.
  An index may use an embedding entry from `adapters.embed`.
- `defaults` (every key is optional):

| setting | default |
|---|---|
| `max_calls` | 40 |
| `max_nudges` | 3 |
| `tool_fail_limit` | 5 |
| `llm_retries` | 3 |
| `retry_wait` | 2.0 |
| `parallel` | 1 |
| `query_top_k` | 5 |
| `query_max_chars` | 4000 |
| `max_index_tools` | 6 |
| `image_max_mb` | 2 |
| `images_per_turn` | 4 |
| `max_iterations` | 3 |

## Common tasks

- **Sketch on a screen:** `nextop studio` opens a local screen to add workers, draw flows and
  set up file servers. It writes skeleton files; fill in the details (schemas, personas, checkers) here.
  To change the screen itself: `nextop studio --copy-page` copies it to `studio/studio.html`, which is
  then served instead of the built-in page (upgrades never touch it).
- **Add a worker:** create `workers/<id>/` with `worker.json` and `persona.md`, then put the
  block into a flow. See `workers/README.md`.
- **Give a worker domain knowledge:** `nextop index --worker <id> --add <folder or .md file>`.
- **Add a tool:** one file `tools/<name>.py`, then list `<name>` in the worker's `tools`.
- **Collect material:** write a tool (search, download, generate) that saves files in `ctx["files_dir"]`;
  the worker then uploads them with `<file_server>_upload`. Keys go in `.env`.
- **Run:** `nextop run --input input.json`; the input goes to the flow's start blocks: start functions
  (`START = True`) and start workers (worker blocks with no incoming line; their worker.json `inputs` define it).
  Resume a failed run with `nextop resume <run_id>`. Files you give (a folder path) are start-function inputs.
- **Human review:** `"review": true` on a worker block (studio: the block's review checkbox; not inside parallel
  sections); decide with `nextop review <run_id> <block> approve|redo --note ...` or on the studio RUNS tab.
- **Branch or loop back:** a switch block with a switch function (its CASES); a back line re-runs earlier
  blocks with feedback, up to `max_iterations`. See flows/README.md and functions/README.md.
- **Send work only where it applies:** mark a worker's output terminals `"optional": true` (a manager with one
  terminal per subordinate); a terminal it leaves out closes its lines, so those blocks are skipped. See
  workers/README.md.
- **Ask a worker:** `nextop ask <worker> "question"` (open question, persona only); `--history FILE` adds the
  chat history (a JSON list of `{"role": "user" | "assistant", "content": "..."}`, oldest first).
- **Three checks:**
  - structure check `nextop check`: the program checks every definition (errors stop the run; warnings and
    suggestions do not). Run it after every change.
  - pre-check `nextop inspect <worker>`: an LLM reads one worker's parts and lists where they no longer agree;
    it writes `workers/<id>/inspect.md`. Read that file first when fixing a worker, then pre-check again.
  - post-check `checks.py`: checks every output the worker saves and refuses it until its rules hold.

## Designing a worker (order)

Change what affects other items first and what is only affected last; the persona comes last.

1. identity: `name`, `title` (used in the persona and in the next block's input headings)
2. output terminals: what it saves (`outputs` with JSON Schemas); receivers and the checker depend on it
3. input: the lines into its block in a flow (decided in the flow, after the senders' outputs)
4. tools: what it can do (`tools`, files in tools/) and, for each, how this worker uses it (`tool_notes`)
5. domain knowledge: what it knows (`knowledge/`)
6. limits: `max_calls`, ...
7. checker: `checks.py`, the rules a schema cannot express, with `RULES` (the same rules in plain words)
8. persona and mission, written last from all of the above

Rules of thumb:
- Schemas: the program checks `type`, `required`, `enum`, `minItems`/`maxItems`, `minLength`/`maxLength`,
  `pattern` and `"additionalProperties": false`, and refuses a save that breaks them. A `description` is only
  read by the LLM (optional): use it when a field's name does not say what goes in, or for a field rule
  ("one sentence"). Write a field's meaning in the schema or the mission, not both.
- Tool usage goes in `tool_notes`, not in the mission: the mission is left out of open questions, the notes are
  not. The same tool is used differently by different workers, so the notes belong to the worker. Every tool in
  `tools` should have notes (the structure check warns otherwise); notes on the program's tools are optional.
- Checkers check form and facts (ids exist, counts, files exist, no forbidden words). Judgement (what is
  good, what to prefer) belongs in the mission, not in the checker.
- One worker, one job. If a persona needs "and also ...", consider a second worker or a function block.
- Work an LLM need not judge (joining files, converting, counting) is a function block, not a worker.

## Debugging a run

When a result is wrong, look at what the worker really got and did, in this order:

1. `runs/<run_id>/blocks/<block>/attempt-<n>/inputs.md`: the exact input the worker received (one section per line).
   Blocks a back line can send again keep `blocks/<block>/iter-<i>/attempt-<n>/` (i: that block's own iteration);
   `switch_log.jsonl` (and each switch block's `iterations.json`) shows every choice and the feedback it sent back.
2. `calls.jsonl` (every LLM request and reply) and `tools.jsonl` (every tool call and result, checker errors included).
3. `output.json`: what it saved. `status.json`: done / failed and why.
4. `nextop studio` > RUNS > BLOCK VIEW shows the same as tables: settings and tools, report input and output,
   file server input and output.

Fix the cause where it lives: a wrong or missing input is the flow or the sender's output; a misunderstood
task is the mission; a broken rule is the checker; a bad tool result is the tool. Then run again from that
block: `nextop resume <run_id> --from <block>` (the blocks before it are kept).
